title: Denver Tech Center (DTC)
name: Denver Tech Center (DTC)
metaTitle: Denver Tech Center 1031 Exchange Services | 1031 Exchange Denver
metaDescription: Denver Tech Center 1031 exchange guidance for suburban Class A and B office campuses, corporate flex space, and I-25 corridor property near Denver.

sections.html: The Denver Tech Center, most people just call it DTC, is the suburban office park strung along I-25 south of downtown Denver. It's corporate campus buildings, mid-rise towers, and surface parking lots, the exact opposite of the walkable brick blocks in LoDo or Cherry Creek North.

sections.heading: A Corridor Built for Cars, Not Sidewalks
sections.html:
DTC grew out from the late 1970s onward as companies moved south along the interstate for cheaper land and easier parking than downtown could offer. That history is still visible in the building stock: low-rise and mid-rise towers set back from the road, surface lots out front, campus landscaping between buildings. It leases differently than downtown too, tenants here expect a parking ratio downtown can't match, and that's a real selling point when a company is deciding where to renew.

Hybrid work has hit this corridor the same way it hit downtown. Some campuses have real vacancy now, and a few owners are exploring flex, lab, or even residential conversion on buildings that were pure office five years ago.

Worth knowing going in: DTC is a brand and a business district identity more than a strict jurisdictional line. The corridor spans parts of Denver proper along with Greenwood Village and touches Centennial to the south, and property tax rates, zoning authority, and even street maintenance responsibility can shift block by block depending on which municipality a specific building sits in.

sections.heading: The Property Types on This List
sections.html:
What actually comes up for sale in DTC:

  • Class A and B suburban office towers along the I-25 corridor
  • corporate campus buildings with structured or surface parking
  • flex and light industrial space on the corridor's edges
  • office buildings being repositioned for medical, lab, or residential use

sections.heading: Light Rail Changed the Leasing Story Here
sections.html:
The RTD light rail line running through DTC gave a handful of buildings near the Orchard and Belleview stations a real leasing edge over campuses that only offer a parking lot. Tenants that want walkable transit access for employees will pay for it, and that premium is one of the clearer, more durable trends in this submarket rather than a temporary fad.

Fiddler's Green Amphitheatre sits on the corridor's east side and draws a large seasonal concert crowd through the summer months. Retail and restaurant space near the venue sees a real bump in traffic on show nights, though that bump is concentrated in a handful of months and shouldn't be treated as a year-round baseline when underwriting nearby retail rents.

sections.heading: Diligence That Matters Here
sections.html:
Check occupancy trend rather than current occupancy alone, since a building sitting at 80 percent today could be sliding from 95 percent or climbing from 60 percent, and those are two very different assets. Confirm parking ratio and any shared-easement parking arrangements between campus buildings under common ownership. And if a seller is marketing a conversion story, get an independent engineer's opinion on floor plate depth and window-to-core ratio before trusting the pro forma.

Power capacity is a growing diligence item too, since some buyers are eyeing older DTC office buildings for lab or light data-center retrofits. Existing electrical service on a 1980s or 1990s tower usually falls well short of what a lab or server-room tenant needs, and upgrading service can mean a utility company queue that runs months longer than a typical construction timeline.

sections.heading: Positioning a DTC Identification
sections.html:
DTC office is a common pairing on identification lists with Cherry Creek or downtown Denver assets, since its lower entry basis and stronger day-one yield can offset a higher-basis, lower-yield property elsewhere on the list. A qualified intermediary should confirm any lender preflight on a DTC deal early, since suburban office underwriting has gotten tighter across the metro over the past several years.

Form 8824 preparation on a DTC exchange usually runs more straightforward than a downtown deal, since suburban office titles tend to have a cleaner, shorter chain of ownership than a century-old building in LoDo or downtown Denver. That said, a tax advisor should still confirm any depreciation recapture exposure on a heavily depreciated suburban office asset before the exchange closes. Rent roll analysis on a DTC campus building should also separate single-tenant floors from multi-tenant floors, since renewal probability and turnover cost differ meaningfully between the two even within the same building.

faqs.q: Is DTC office overbuilt right now?
faqs.a: Some campuses carry real vacancy, others near light rail stations lease well. Check occupancy trend over the trailing two to three years, not a single point-in-time snapshot.

faqs.q: Does proximity to light rail actually change DTC office value?
faqs.a: Yes, buildings near the Orchard and Belleview stations have leased at a premium over pure drive-to campuses further from a stop, and that gap has held up rather than faded.

faqs.q: Can a DTC office building be converted to residential or lab space?
faqs.a: Some can, depending on floor plate depth and window access. Get an independent structural and mechanical review before assuming a conversion pencils out on any specific building.

faqs.q: How does DTC office typically pair with other Denver-area identifications?
faqs.a: Its lower entry basis and stronger current yield often offset a higher-basis property like Cherry Creek retail, giving the overall exchange a more balanced cash flow profile.

faqs.q: What financing issue comes up most with DTC office deals?
faqs.a: Lenders have tightened suburban office underwriting metro-wide, so get a lender preflight done early rather than waiting until late in the 45-day identification window.
